P1.studentBookTitle: REB Primary Mathematics P1 Student Book (SB)
P1.teacherGuideTitle: REB Primary Mathematics P1 Teacher's Guide (TG)

units.keyUnitCompetence: Develop number sense up to 20 and perform simple operations of addition and subtraction within 20.

lessons.lessonTitle: Counting and Reading Whole Numbers from 1 to 20
lessons.instrObjective: Using number cards and real classroom objects, learners should be able to count, read, and write whole numbers from 1 to 20 correctly without hesitation.
lessons.materials: Number cards (1-20), chalkboard, counters, bottle caps, small sticks, Manila paper, REB P1 Student Book pp. 12-16
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P1 Student Book (SB), Unit 1, pp. 12-16; REB P1 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 8-11; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw/course/index.php?categoryid=19)
lessons.intro: Teacher greets the class and sings a short counting rhyme from 1 to 10 with learners. Teacher shows 5 bottle caps and asks learners to count aloud together, activating prior knowledge of numbers.
lessons.development: Teacher models counting objects up to 20 on the teacher's table. Learners work in small groups of 4 with counters to make groups of 10, 15, and 20. Teacher circulates to assist learners with SEN by providing tactile number cards and guiding their hand counting. Selected learners come to the chalkboard to write numbers corresponding to groups of counters drawn by the teacher.
lessons.conclusion: Teacher leads a quick class recap where learners count aloud from 20 backwards to 1. Teacher praises correct participation and clarifies any confusion between numbers like 12 and 20.
lessons.evaluation: Learners complete Exercise 1 in REB P1 Student Book page 15: matching drawn object sets with correct number symbols from 1 to 20. Teacher checks notebooks and provides immediate remedial feedback.

lessons.lessonTitle: Addition of Whole Numbers within 20 using Concrete Objects
lessons.instrObjective: Using counters and number lines, learners should be able to add two single-digit numbers with sums up to 20 accurately and explain their steps.
lessons.materials: Counters, counting sticks, ten-frames, number cards, REB P1 Student Book pp. 18-22
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P1 Student Book (SB), Unit 1, pp. 18-22; REB P1 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 14-17; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw/course/index.php?categoryid=19)
lessons.intro: Teacher displays two small baskets with 6 sticks in one and 4 in another. Teacher asks: 'How many sticks do we have in total if we combine both baskets?' Learners share ideas.
lessons.development: Teacher demonstrates addition as combining sets using counters on the table and writing the horizontal addition equation on the chalkboard (e.g., 8 + 5 = 13). In pairs, learners practice adding sets of counters and recording equations in their exercise books. Teacher provides differentiated support for SEN learners by using a physical 20-bead abacus.
lessons.conclusion: Two pairs demonstrate their addition method on the chalkboard while the rest of the class verifies the answer by clapping.
lessons.evaluation: Short oral and written assessment: 5 simple addition problems on the chalkboard (e.g., 7 + 6, 9 + 4). Teacher inspects exercise books.

units.keyUnitCompetence: Recognise, name, and draw basic two-dimensional shapes (squares, rectangles, triangles, circles) in the environment.

lessons.lessonTitle: Identifying Squares, Rectangles, Triangles, and Circles
lessons.instrObjective: Using paper cutouts and classroom objects, learners should be able to identify, name, and sort basic 2D shapes correctly.
lessons.materials: Cardboard shape cutouts, rulers, scissors, classroom objects (books, clocks), REB P1 Student Book pp. 45-48
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P1 Student Book (SB), Unit 2, pp. 45-48; REB P1 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 30-33; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw)
lessons.intro: Teacher shows a classroom clock and a textbook, asking learners to describe their outline shapes.
lessons.development: Teacher introduces square, rectangle, triangle, and circle cutouts, explaining their features (corners and sides). Learners in small groups sort mixed paper shapes into matching piles and find matching shapes around the classroom.
lessons.conclusion: Learners share which shapes they discovered in the classroom environment and explain why a circle is different from a square.
lessons.evaluation: Worksheet: color all triangles green, circles red, squares blue, and rectangles yellow.

P2.studentBookTitle: REB Primary Mathematics P2 Student Book (SB)
P2.teacherGuideTitle: REB Primary Mathematics P2 Teacher's Guide (TG)

units.keyUnitCompetence: Read, write, count, compare, and represent whole numbers up to 100 in terms of tens and ones.

lessons.lessonTitle: Place Value of Numbers up to 100 (Tens and Ones)
lessons.instrObjective: Using bundles of 10 sticks and loose sticks, learners should be able to decompose 2-digit numbers into tens and ones correctly.
lessons.materials: Bundles of 10 sticks, rubber bands, place-value table chart, number cards, REB P2 Student Book pp. 10-14
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P2 Student Book (SB), Unit 1, pp. 10-14; REB P2 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 8-12; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw/course/index.php?categoryid=19)
lessons.intro: Teacher asks learners to count from 10 to 50 by tens (10, 20, 30...). Teacher displays 3 bundles of 10 sticks and 4 single sticks and asks how many sticks are shown in total.
lessons.development: Teacher introduces the Place Value Chart (Tens | Ones) on the chalkboard. Teacher explains that 34 has 3 Tens and 4 Ones. Learners work in pairs with counting sticks to build numbers called out by the teacher (e.g., 47, 62, 85). Teacher gives learners with SEN color-coded tens and ones cards to reinforce the concept visually and tactilely.
lessons.conclusion: Teacher invites three learners to write numbers on the chalkboard place-value chart and explain their tens and ones digits.
lessons.evaluation: Learners complete Exercise 2 in REB P2 Student Book p. 13: writing tens and ones for given 2-digit numbers (e.g., 58 = ___ Tens and ___ Ones).

lessons.lessonTitle: Comparing Whole Numbers up to 100 using Greater Than, Less Than, and Equal To
lessons.instrObjective: Using number lines and comparison symbols (>, <, =), learners should be able to compare pairs of 2-digit numbers accurately.
lessons.materials: Number line chart, symbol cards (>, <, =), counters, REB P2 Student Book pp. 22-26
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P2 Student Book (SB), Unit 1, pp. 22-26; REB P2 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 18-21; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw)
lessons.intro: Teacher writes 45 and 54 on the chalkboard and asks the class which number is larger and how they know.
lessons.development: Teacher demonstrates how to compare tens digits first, then ones digits, using the symbols >, <, and =. In mixed-gender groups, learners play a card comparison game where each learner draws two number cards and places the correct comparison symbol between them. Teacher monitors and ensures equal speaking time for boys and girls.
lessons.conclusion: Class reviews 5 tricky pairs on the chalkboard (e.g., 79 vs 81, 60 vs 60) and explains the rule.
lessons.evaluation: Individual written exercise: insert >, <, or = in 6 number pairs in exercise books.

units.keyUnitCompetence: Understand and represent 1/2, 1/4, and whole numbers using symmetrical objects and paper folding.

lessons.lessonTitle: Recognizing and Dividing Objects into Halves (1/2)
lessons.instrObjective: Using paper folding and fruit models, learners should be able to divide whole shapes into two equal halves and write 1/2 correctly.
lessons.materials: Paper circles and rectangles, safe plastic scissors, drawings of fruits, REB P2 Student Book pp. 60-64
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P2 Student Book (SB), Unit 2, pp. 60-64; REB P2 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 45-48; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw)
lessons.intro: Teacher shows a whole paper circle and asks how two friends can share it equally without fighting.
lessons.development: Teacher demonstrates folding a circular paper in half and cutting along the fold, showing that two equal parts make a whole (1/2 + 1/2 = 1). Learners practice folding rectangle and square paper sheets into halves in pairs. Teacher emphasizes that both parts must be exactly equal in size.
lessons.conclusion: Learners hold up their folded shapes and explain why unequal pieces are not halves.
lessons.evaluation: Worksheet: tick shapes that are cut into two equal halves and shade 1/2 of each shape.

P3.studentBookTitle: REB Primary Mathematics P3 Student Book (SB)
P3.teacherGuideTitle: REB Primary Mathematics P3 Teacher's Guide (TG)

units.keyUnitCompetence: Read, write, compare, and perform addition and subtraction of whole numbers up to 1,000 in real-life contexts.

lessons.lessonTitle: Reading, Writing, and Place Value of Numbers up to 1,000
lessons.instrObjective: Using place-value abacus charts and base-ten blocks, learners should be able to identify hundreds, tens, and ones in 3-digit numbers correctly.
lessons.materials: Base-ten blocks, wooden abacus, place value cards (Hundreds, Tens, Ones), REB P3 Student Book pp. 8-13
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P3 Student Book (SB), Unit 1, pp. 8-13; REB P3 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 6-10; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw/course/index.php?categoryid=19)
lessons.intro: Teacher asks learners to count by 100s up to 500 (100, 200, 300...). Teacher writes 345 on the chalkboard and asks learners what each digit stands for.
lessons.development: Teacher demonstrates representing 345 on a 3-spike abacus (3 Hundreds, 4 Tens, 5 Ones). In groups of 5, learners use number cards to construct 3-digit numbers called out by the teacher and decompose them into expanded form (300 + 40 + 5). Teacher supports SEN learners by using large print number flashcards and physical base-ten blocks.
lessons.conclusion: Learners volunteer to come to the front and challenge the class to read a 3-digit number they have formed on the abacus.
lessons.evaluation: Exercise in REB P3 Student Book p. 12: Write 5 given numbers in words and in expanded place value form.

lessons.instrObjective: Using standard vertical column addition and place-value charts, learners should be able to add two 3-digit numbers with carrying correctly.
lessons.materials: Place value grid charts, number flashcards, REB P3 Student Book pp. 24-28
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P3 Student Book (SB), Unit 1, pp. 24-28; REB P3 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 18-22; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw)
lessons.intro: Teacher writes a review problem without carrying (e.g., 234 + 142) on the chalkboard for a quick 2-minute warm-up.
lessons.development: Teacher introduces a problem requiring regrouping: 368 + 257. Teacher models step-by-step column addition on the chalkboard, showing how 8 ones + 7 ones = 15 ones (write 5 ones and carry 1 ten to the tens column). Learners practice in pairs with 4 similar problems, discussing their carrying steps cooperatively without rushing each other.
lessons.conclusion: Teacher selects two pairs to demonstrate their worked solutions on the chalkboard and explain the carrying step clearly.
lessons.evaluation: Individual written evaluation: solve 4 column addition problems with carrying in exercise books.

units.unitTitle: Multiplication and Division Tables up to 10
units.keyUnitCompetence: Master multiplication tables up to 10x10 and perform division as inverse multiplication.

lessons.instrObjective: Using counters arranged in rows and columns (arrays), learners should be able to calculate multiplication products accurately and explain multiplication as repeated addition.
lessons.materials: Counters, grid paper, multiplication chart, REB P3 Student Book pp. 52-56
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P3 Student Book (SB), Unit 3, pp. 52-56; REB P3 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 38-42; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw)
lessons.intro: Teacher shows 4 groups of 3 bottle caps and asks: 'How many bottle caps are there? Can we find the total without counting one by one?'
lessons.development: Teacher explains 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12 is the same as 4 x 3 = 12. Learners work in mixed-gender groups to build rectangular arrays using counters on their desks for 5 x 4, 3 x 6, and 4 x 7. Teacher ensures equal participation of boys and girls during array construction.
lessons.conclusion: Class recites the multiplication patterns for 2, 3, 4, and 5 together and reflects on how arrays make counting faster.
lessons.evaluation: Worksheet: Convert 5 repeated addition sentences into multiplication equations and solve.

P4.studentBookTitle: REB Primary Mathematics P4 Student Book (SB)
P4.teacherGuideTitle: REB Primary Mathematics P4 Teacher's Guide (TG)

units.keyUnitCompetence: Read, write, compare, and round whole numbers up to 100,000 and apply operations in daily life.

lessons.lessonTitle: Place Value and Value of Digits up to 100,000
lessons.instrObjective: Using place value charts up to Ten Thousands, learners should be able to identify the place value and numeric value of each digit in a 5-digit number correctly.
lessons.materials: Place value table (Ten Thousands, Thousands, Hundreds, Tens, Ones), number flashcards, REB P4 Student Book pp. 14-19
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P4 Student Book (SB), Unit 1, pp. 14-19; REB P4 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 10-14; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw/course/index.php?categoryid=19)
lessons.intro: Teacher asks learners to read 9,999 on the chalkboard, then asks what number comes next when we add 1.
lessons.development: Teacher introduces 10,000 and expands the place value chart to 5 columns. Teacher writes 64,825 and guides learners to state the place value of 6 (Ten Thousands) and its value (60,000). In groups, learners draw 5-digit place value tables on Manila paper and represent numbers given by the teacher. Teacher provides enlarged digit cards for SEN learners with visual difficulties.
lessons.conclusion: Learners summarize the difference between 'place value' (name of the column) and 'value' (number of units).
lessons.evaluation: REB P4 Student Book p. 18 Exercise 1: State the place value and value of the underlined digits in 6 given 5-digit numbers.

units.keyUnitCompetence: Understand, compare, and perform basic operations on proper fractions, mixed numbers, and simple decimals.

lessons.lessonTitle: Identifying and Comparing Proper, Improper Fractions, and Mixed Numbers
lessons.instrObjective: Using fraction strips and circular models, learners should be able to distinguish between proper fractions, improper fractions, and mixed numbers accurately.
lessons.materials: Fraction strips, cardboard circular pies, colored markers, REB P4 Student Book pp. 68-73
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P4 Student Book (SB), Unit 5, pp. 68-73; REB P4 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 50-55; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw/course/index.php?categoryid=19)
lessons.intro: Teacher displays 3 equal paper loaves of bread and asks how 2 learners can share 3 loaves equally.
lessons.development: Teacher explains proper fractions (numerator < denominator, e.g., 3/4), improper fractions (numerator >= denominator, e.g., 5/4), and mixed numbers (whole number + fraction, e.g., 1 1/4). Learners work in small groups with paper models to convert 5/4 into 1 1/4 by combining whole circles and remaining quarters.
lessons.conclusion: Learners explain the relationship between improper fractions and mixed numbers on the chalkboard.
lessons.evaluation: Exercise: Classify a list of 10 fractions into Proper, Improper, or Mixed Numbers in exercise books.

lessons.lessonTitle: Addition and Subtraction of Fractions with Like Denominators
lessons.instrObjective: Using shaded fraction bars, learners should be able to add and subtract proper fractions with the same denominator correctly.
lessons.materials: Fraction bars, grid paper, colored pencils, REB P4 Student Book pp. 76-80
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P4 Student Book (SB), Unit 5, pp. 76-80; REB P4 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 58-62; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw)
lessons.intro: Teacher draws a rectangle divided into 5 equal parts on the board, shades 2 parts green and 1 part blue, and asks what fraction is shaded in total.
lessons.development: Teacher establishes the rule: to add or subtract fractions with the same denominator, add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same (e.g., 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7). Learners practice with word problems involving sharing garden plots and resources.
lessons.conclusion: Teacher asks: 'Why don't we add the denominators together?' Class discusses and clarifies.
lessons.evaluation: Written assessment: Solve 5 addition and subtraction fraction equations with like denominators.

P5.studentBookTitle: REB Primary Mathematics P5 Student Book (SB)
P5.teacherGuideTitle: REB Primary Mathematics P5 Teacher's Guide (TG)

units.unitTitle: Whole Numbers up to 1,000,000 (LCM and GCF)
units.keyUnitCompetence: Read, write, compare, and perform operations on numbers up to 1,000,000; find Prime Numbers, LCM, and GCF.

lessons.lessonTitle: Finding Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) and Greatest Common Factor (GCF) using Prime Factorization
lessons.instrObjective: Using factor trees and prime factorization tables, learners should be able to calculate the LCM and GCF of two or three whole numbers correctly.
lessons.materials: Factor tree charts, multiplication tables, REB P5 Student Book pp. 20-25
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P5 Student Book (SB), Unit 1, pp. 20-25; REB P5 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 15-20; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw/course/index.php?categoryid=19)
lessons.intro: Teacher writes the numbers 12 and 18 on the board and asks learners to list all numbers that divide 12 without a remainder.
lessons.development: Teacher demonstrates prime factorization using factor trees for 12 (2 x 2 x 3) and 18 (2 x 3 x 3). Teacher explains how to extract GCF (common prime factors = 2 x 3 = 6) and LCM (highest powers = 36). In groups of 4, learners solve real-life problems involving recurring events (e.g., two buses departing every 15 and 20 mins). Teacher assists SEN learners with clear step-by-step division ladders.
lessons.conclusion: Learners present their factor trees on the chalkboard and explain the practical difference between LCM and GCF.
lessons.evaluation: REB P5 Student Book p. 24 Exercise 3: Calculate the GCF and LCM for three pairs of numbers (16 and 24; 20 and 30; 18 and 27).

units.keyUnitCompetence: Understand percentages, convert between fractions, decimals, and percentages, and calculate simple interest in financial contexts.

lessons.lessonTitle: Converting between Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages
lessons.instrObjective: Using 100-square grids, learners should be able to convert fractions and decimals to percentages and vice-versa accurately.
lessons.materials: 100-square grid sheets, colored markers, calculator, REB P5 Student Book pp. 62-67
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P5 Student Book (SB), Unit 3, pp. 62-67; REB P5 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 48-52; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw)
lessons.intro: Teacher asks learners where they have seen the symbol '%' in daily life (e.g., shop discounts, test scores, bank savings).
lessons.development: Teacher explains that 'percent' means 'out of 100' (e.g., 25% = 25/100 = 1/4 = 0.25). Learners work in pairs shading 100-grid sheets to represent 20%, 50%, 75%, and 10% and record the equivalent fractions and decimals in a table. Teacher connects percentage savings to good financial habits.
lessons.conclusion: Class completes a rapid chalkboard conversion drill matching percentage cards to fraction cards.
lessons.evaluation: Worksheet: Complete a 5-row conversion table (Fraction | Decimal | Percentage).

P6.studentBookTitle: REB Primary Mathematics P6 Student Book (SB)
P6.teacherGuideTitle: REB Primary Mathematics P6 Teacher's Guide (TG)

units.unitTitle: Whole Numbers up to 10,000,000 (Powers, Indices, and Roots)
units.keyUnitCompetence: Read, write, compare, and apply operations on numbers up to 10,000,000; solve problems involving indices and square roots.

lessons.lessonTitle: Powers, Indices, and Calculating Square Roots of Perfect Squares
lessons.instrObjective: Using prime factorization, learners should be able to express numbers in index notation and calculate square roots of perfect squares accurately.
lessons.materials: Square grid paper, prime factorization charts, scientific calculator (for verification), REB P6 Student Book pp. 15-21
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P6 Student Book (SB), Unit 1, pp. 15-21; REB P6 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 12-16; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw/course/index.php?categoryid=19)
lessons.intro: Teacher draws a 4x4 square on grid paper and asks learners to count the total squares (16). Teacher explains 4 squared = 4 x 4 = 16.
lessons.development: Teacher introduces square root notation and models finding the square root of 144 using prime factorization (144 = 2^4 x 3^2, square root = 2^2 x 3 = 12). In small groups, learners find square roots of 196, 225, and 400 using prime factor trees. Teacher supports SEN learners by providing visual reference tables of squares from 1x1 to 15x15.
lessons.conclusion: Learners explain the inverse relationship between squaring a number and finding its square root.
lessons.evaluation: REB P6 Student Book p. 20 Exercise 2: Calculate the square root of 5 given perfect squares using prime factorization.

units.unitTitle: Introductory Algebra and Simple Linear Equations
units.keyUnitCompetence: Form and solve simple linear equations and algebraic expressions involving one variable in real-world contexts.

lessons.lessonTitle: Forming and Solving Simple Linear Equations in One Variable
lessons.instrObjective: Using balance scale models, learners should be able to form and solve simple linear equations of the form ax + b = c correctly.
lessons.materials: Physical balance scale, weights/counters, algebra cards, REB P6 Student Book pp. 88-93
lessons.references: REB Primary Mathematics P6 Student Book (SB), Unit 4, pp. 88-93; REB P6 Teacher's Guide (TG), pp. 68-72; REB e-Learning Portal (elearning.reb.rw/course/index.php?categoryid=19)
lessons.intro: Teacher displays a two-pan balance scale with a mystery box on one side and weights on the other, asking what must be done to keep the scale balanced.
lessons.development: Teacher introduces variables (e.g., x) to represent unknown quantities and explains the golden rule of algebra: whatever operation is performed on one side of an equation must be performed on the other side to maintain balance (e.g., solve 2x + 5 = 15). Learners practice in pairs solving 4 equations and checking their solutions by substitution.
lessons.conclusion: Two learners demonstrate solving 3x - 4 = 11 on the chalkboard, explaining each balancing step.
lessons.evaluation: Written quiz: Solve 5 linear equations in one variable and verify the answer.
